name: Arame-Gubaare
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Only lexicostatistical/classification notes (Barry 1987; Dabo 2013; Pozdniakov & Segerer 2024); no grammar or phonology of any kind located

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page Arame-Gubaare (aram1260) and reference records 65308 (Barry 1987) and 548246 (Dabo 2013).
sources.note: No descriptive references attached (0). Justification note: Barry 1987: 72 lexicostatistics shows the Guinea-Bissau varieties too divergent from Kugere-Kuxinge to be intelligible; cf. Dabo 2013; Pozdniakov & Segerer 2024. Barry 1987 record maps variety code 'Gb Gubaare' to aram1260; Dabo 2013 record maps 'Édammé in NW Guinea Bissau' to aram1260.

sources.citation: Dabo, Mamadou. 2024. La négation en joola edamme (langue atlantique du nord-ouest de la Guinée-Bissau). Collection Thèse/Synthèse 4(11), Éditions Francophones Universitaires d'Afrique, pp. 75-88.
sources.note: Nothing. Negation morphosyntax only; sec. 1 'Généralités' covers noun classes and subject indices; no accent/stress/tone mention anywhere (the word 'syllabe' occurs once, p. 84, about the vowel of the infix -hami-). Cites the author's 300-page UCAD thesis (Dabo 2013: 141-146) as the description of the language.

sources.citation: Thornell, Christina. 2020. Milieu langagier chez les Bayotte au Sénégal, aujourd'hui et dans l'avenir. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2020-006. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing on stress (sociolinguistic survey). Identity value: secs. 2.2.1.3-2.2.2.2 (pp. 5-6) equate Barry's 'gubaare' with the codification decree's 'kúsikinay' (the Guinea-Bissau Bayot dialect, called kuhoole by Senegalese Bayot); Dabo (2013) treats Guinea-Bissau Bayot as one dialect named aramé/édammé; sec. 6 (~p. 70) states the only linguistic work on this variety is Dabo's 2013 UCAD thesis and that Guinea-Bissau-produced studies were not accessible to the author. Lexical similarity Senegal vs Guinea-Bissau dialects 53-57% (Barry 1987: 72).

Nothing on phonology. Name the Guinea-Bissau dialects Arame (= Edamme) and Gubaare (en) / Kúsikinay with villages Edame (Érame), Élia, Kásu, Kuţaaze, Ñaḃan, Ñambalã Muxumo (fr); fr bibliography lists Barry 1987, Carlton & Rand 1993/1994, Diagne 2009/2016, Kennedy 1964, Tastevin 1936 — all Senegal-side or wordlist/survey items.
